full_judgment: 4. Opposite Party Nos.1 to 5 of this Civil Revisional petition as plaintiffs laid a suit being Title Suit No.126 of 1974 in the Fifth Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for declaration of title on the property described in schedule to the plaint and also for a decree of khas possession on removing construction constructed thereon. The said suit was renumbered as Title Suit No. 298 of 1992 on transfer to the Court of Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka. Averments made in the plaint are that Md Yasin Bepari had been owner and possessor of the property recorded in Cadestral Survey Khatian Nos.10 and 11. Md Yasin Bepari died leaving behind two sons, Abdul Hamid and Amirullah and three daughters Jiashbi Bibi, Hashrabi Bibi and Nanna Bibi and wife Anrabi Bibi, and sons, daughters and wife became owners and possessors of the said property. Abdul Hamid, the heir son of Md Yasin Bepari, became owner and possessor of the property of Cadestral Survey plot No.8587 of Cadestral Survey Khatian Nos.10 and 11 measuring 2.46 acres by way of several deeds of transfer from other heirs of Md Yasin Bepari. Abdul Hamid Bepari, thereafter, transferred the said 2.46 acres of property in favour of predecessor mother of the plaintiffs, Syeda Salima Noorjahan Begum by a deed of conveyance dated 13-9-1932. On the death of Syeda Salima Noorjahan Begum, plaintiffs as legal heirs inherited the said property and remained owners and possessors of the said property. Defendants got no title and possession over that 2.46 acres of property. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 on the strength of sale deed dated 1-1-1971 from Jumratan Bibi, alleged daughter of Md Yasin Bepari, entered unauthorisedly on the property described in schedule-Kha to the plaint. The schedule Kha property will be referred to hereinafter as suit property. Md Yasin Bepari got no daughter named Jumratan Bibi. The deed of defendants are forged, fraudulent and on the basis of that deed defendants did not acquire any title on the suit property.
